lines.text: David asks God to deliver him from his enemies when Saul sends men to watch his house in order to kill him.
David says fierce men lie in wait for him without sin of his own, and asks God to show no mercy to wicked traitors.
His enemies return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the wilderness, and they say, "Who can hear us?"
David asks God not to kill them, or his people will forget, so it may be known to Egypt that God rules over Jacob.
David says he will sing of God's strength in the morning, because God is his fortress and refuge in times of trouble.
